text:
Maya H: Hey all — first day! On an M1 Pro Mac and hitting a few snags getting the dev env bootstrapped. Installed Homebrew to /opt/homebrew and asdf via git in ~/.asdf. When I run `asdf install nodejs 18.16.0` it fails with a gpg/import error. Any quick tips?

Alex W: Welcome Maya! For asdf nodejs you often need to import the Node release team keyring first. Try: `bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring` then `asdf install nodejs 18.16.0`.
Also, ensure Homebrew is on your PATH early: add `export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH` to your shell rc (or the fish equivalent).

Maya H: Thanks — I'm on fish shell and using direnv/direnvrc from the dotfiles. Where should I put the PATH config for fish? Also trying to install rust/cargo — rustup seems to pick the x86 installer and fails.

Devon P: For fish add `set -gx PATH /opt/homebrew/bin $PATH` in `~/.config/fish/config.fish`. For rust on Apple Silicon run the rustup script and it should detect aarch64: `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh`. If you see x86 bits, make sure your terminal isn't running under Rosetta.

Maya H: How do I check if my terminal is under Rosetta? Also direnv is refusing to load .envrc with an error about `layout asdf` not found.

Sam I: Open Finder -> Applications -> Utilities -> Terminal, right-click -> Get Info, and make sure "Open using Rosetta" is unchecked.
For direnv + asdf on fish, you need to source the asdf fish integration before the direnv hook. Example `~/.config/fish/config.fish` snippet: 

```
# ~/.config/fish/config.fish
set -gx PATH /opt/homebrew/bin $PATH
source ~/.asdf/asdf.fish
eval (direnv hook fish)
```

That ordering is important so `layout asdf` is available when direnv evaluates .envrc.

Maya H: That ordering fixed the node gpg/import step — thanks! Last couple q's: our README mentions setting `RUSTFLAGS` and `CGO_ENABLED=1` for some packages. Should I set those globally or per-project? Also our projects use go modules and some native libs need cgo.

Devon P: Prefer per-project via `.envrc` to avoid surprising global builds. Typical entries we recommend (in `.envrc`):

```
export RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native"
export CGO_ENABLED=1
export GOPATH=$HOME/go
export PATH=$GOPATH/bin:$PATH
```

Note: on mac arm, `-C target-cpu=native` can make builds non-portable if you build locally and deploy to linux; consider leaving it out for reproducibility. For Go, `brew install go` is fine and then `mkdir -p $GOPATH/src`.

Maya H: Good point about portability. One more: who should I ping about getting my dotfiles synced and access to the KMS secrets mentioned in onboarding? I forked the dotfiles but can't find the 1Password entry. @devon P?

Devon P: Ping me or @Alex W and we'll spin up the dotfiles sync. Secrets live in 1Password under the tag `redwood/new-hire`. Infra will need to approve KMS access; I've asked them to create a ticket when you're ready. Also check the devex onboarding doc: https://redwood-internal/handbook/devex/onboarding
